label: What could lack being could lack each act it has
paraphrase: OPEN analyst premise, attribution deferred: if x could lack its act as to being (CanLack x esse, definition 56b438a0) and x is in act in respect r, then x could lack its act in r. Strongest support: 7067553d, nothing has actuality except insofar as it is; if x could be without being, it could be without whatever act it has. The premise fixes a uniform reading of the primitive CanLack: 'could be without the act, including by not being'. On a rival reading for respects other than esse, 'could exist while lacking the act', it fails for the essential acts of a contingent thing (a contingent thing that cannot exist without an essential property), so the two readings of CanLack must not be mixed; 'could lack being' is coherent only on the inclusive reading. It takes no stand on which things could lack being.
